page: Amazon Web Services m9g.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is absent. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and utilizes the arm64 architecture. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9g.16xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 127,950.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 30,217.0. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, reaching a top-tier 9,281.17 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and strong large-block read/write speeds. The instance also excels in data processing tasks, achieving top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and static web serving throughput at 179.08 GB/sec. However, single-core stress-ng performance and encryption capabilities fall into the average tier, and LLM text generation speeds for small models are poor, registering at 9.76 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.16xlarge offers high resource density and strong benchmark-per-resource tradeoffs for multi-threaded workloads due to its dedicated physical core architecture and high memory bandwidth. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and Redis deployments, while being less optimal for workloads requiring local NVMe storage, GPU acceleration, or high-speed LLM text generation.
